title: MV/MZ When Will RPG Maker MZ Run On Linux Like RPG Maker MV?

posts.author: savantsavior
posts.body:
Hi,
I just purchased RPG Maker MV/MZ bundle on Steam.
When will RPG Maker MZ run on Linux like RPG Maker MV?
Let me know, thank you...
SS

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
personally, I doubt that it ever will.
it takes time and work to convert a program to a new OS, even if it already works on similar OS. And every company will have to calculate if the added number of customers from a new OS can bring in enough venue to warrant that work.
By now, MZ has been out and stable long enough that they should have been able to do that conversion if they thought it would bring in enough revenue to be worth it.
I think they tested the waters for both MacOS and Linux with MV, but only the MacOS added enough users and the Linux version isn't used enough to warrant the work in their calculations.

I have a Steam Deck and bought RPG Maker MZ a few weeks ago and it runs fine (sorta) so the game's help pop ups (when you hover the mouse over something to get help) are buggy unless you run it on proton experimental, and this was the real kicker- you can't find the file the main Project installs to in the Linux files...
Let me word this differently, when you click "new project" it lets you choose a location- ya for a Windows computer.... So if you choose "documents" like I did, it's not in the Linux document folder, it's in a
Windows document folder
(I have no clue where my 1st or second project are lol
Here's how to make it work (again at least on steamdeck)
Buy a SanDisk SD card and put it in, now choose the location you want your project to be in the SD card, NOW it should be accessible! I guess an SD card is the only file location shared between a Linux and Windows lol
Here's some extra advice, if you want the program efseeker to work (because that's what runs the effects of the game), it sorta doesn't work too well on Linux because you can't upload into a SD card (or not that I found lol) however, you can get the window version and: 1. Run efseeker on wine (works fine) 2. Make a folder on your desktop- for the example let's call it: #eff 3. Drag the effects folder from your rpgmz project on the SD card into the #eff folder on your desktop 4. Drag all the effects you want to use into the
effects folder's propper location
not just the #eff folder 5. now use whatever you want in the efseeker program, save as a .efkefc into your
Effects folder
not into just the #eff folder 6. Drag the effects folder back into your project folder, and now you have a new custom working effect!
TLDR: RPG maker MZ works fine on Linux running on the right proton, and installed on an SD card- has a few hiccups but nothing that's gonna make you say "this is impossible" (but if you want something that works, just use RPG maker MV- that has its own set of issues but it's already too long of a post to explain lol
Sorry if this was a long post and also half was about efseeker lol... but I hope that answers your question

posts.author: matthew30903
posts.body:
MZ works fairly well using Proton 9.0-4.
I've noticed Wine/Proton sometimes has issues rendering RPG Maker under Xwayland if you are using Nvidia graphics, but it works well enough. Occasionally the drop down menus will look garbled or blank, but closing the menu and opening it back up fixes the issue the majority of the time. Under X11 it seems to work more consistently.
RPG Maker MZ was never made with a native Linux version, but as long as you are okay with a little tinkering around (something you need to be if you want to make games in RPG Maker) it should work. Just make sure you are running fairly up to date graphics drivers and you should have no problem. Older drivers and versions of Proton seemed to cause crashes for me.
Also under Proton it seems MZ has some kind of memory issue as it uses far more memory that it should, never tried MZ on Windows though so that might just be expected behavior.
